thread.title: Close Update: Wall Street Surges Ahead With Dow Hitting January High on Easing Trade Fears

author: MT Newswires
title: Close Update: Wall Street Surges Ahead With Dow Hitting January High on Easing Trade Fears
text:
Shutterstock photo Wall Street forged ahead on Tuesday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average surging more than 180 points into the close amid relief that the latest round in trade-war salvos between the U.S. and China wasn't as bad as investors feared.
Boeing ( BA ) and Caterpillar ( CAT ) were among the best gainers on the blue-chip Dow as trade-sensitive industrials rose 0.9% in the strongest increase on the S&P 500 after consumer discretionary, which was 1.2% stronger.
The announcement from the White House late Monday that the U.S. would hit China with 10% levies on $200 billion of imports -- a tax that rises to 25% in January -- was met with gains in global stocks as it was viewed as milder than it could have been. The worries continued to fade as China said it would retaliate with $60 billion in levies on U.S. goods.
Tariffs on Chinese goods imposed by the U.S. have yet to have much of an effect on the world's biggest economy on a broad economic level, but risks remain if talks between the countries remain "tentative," according to Peter Donisanu, investment strategy analyst with Wells Fargo Investment Institute.
The Dow rallied to the highest level since late January, with more than two-thirds of the components advancing. Apart from the industrial names, Nike ( NKE ) jumped 2.4% after Canaccord said a survey showed most had a positive view of the company after its controversial ad featuring former NFL quarterback Colin Kaepernick.
Among the S&P's sectors, information technology rose 0.6% by the close on a strong day for chip stocks and as Apple ( AAPL ) and Amazon.com ( AMZN ) received Monday's losses. Netflix (NFLX) jumped 4.9% after the streaming service matched AT&T's (T) HBO for 23 Emmy Awards.
The day's economic data was light, with the the National Association of Home Builders' housing market index holding at 67 in September, unchanged from August and the lowest since a year ago.
